768P: Looks digitally upscaled: slightly crunchy/over-sharpened beard and skin texture, mild mushy detail in eyes, teeth a bit blobby and merge into a white band
Framed much closer, so face has more pixels than the others, which flatters its sharpness
No waxy skin; teeth stable across consecutive frames
1440p-sr: Dark ink-like outline around beard strands and jaw edge (SR halo/posterised look), visible at native, faint at half scale
Mouth interior very dark with high-contrast teeth; teeth edges clean, no smearing across 3 consecutive frames
Skin slightly smoothed but not waxy; no shimmer seen
2K: Cleanest, most natural skin and beard gradients, no halos; slightly soft in the teeth and eyes
Eyes half-lidded in sampled frames (performance, not quality); face smallest in frame so fewer face pixels at phone size
No shimmer, waxy skin or teeth smearing seen in 3 consecutive frames

sr_vs_768: Modestly better. SR looks less crunchy and framing is wider, but it adds dark outline halos on beard edges. At phone size (half scale) the difference is small and a viewer would not say one is clearly sharper.
full2k_vs_sr: Slightly cleaner (no halos, more natural texture) but not visibly sharper at phone size, and its face is smaller in frame. Not enough to justify 2.9x the price for talking-head clips.
recommendation: 1440p-sr for final face clips (good value; 768P acceptable for drafts). Reserve full 2K for hero shots only. Caveat: single sample per tier, different performances and framing.
summary: At phone size all three read as sharp, real faces; differences are subtle. 768P scores 6 (crunchy, upscaled look, but closest framing), 1440p-sr 7 (cleaner but dark halos on beard edges), 2K 7.5 (most natural, no halos, but softer teeth and smaller face). 1440p-sr is modestly better than 768P; 2K is only marginally better than 1440p-sr and does not justify 2.9x the cost. No shimmer, waxy skin or teeth smearing found in consecutive frames. Recommend 1440p-sr.
